slice: Slice 3 — graph build-2: predicate-aware graph projection (fetch_graph key-honoring, --edge predicate selection, chain predicate retention, SCC/cycle census, dangling/orphan partition)
thesis: The graph lens (`--lens graph`) is a composition lens whose own `fetch(vertex_path, kind, observer)` silently drops `--key` and conflates every unresolved edge into one `dangling` counter. This slice widens `fetch_graph` to honor `--key` (honor-or-refuse, never silent-drop), adds an `--edge` predicate selector, retains edge-predicate labels through the chain DFS (they are already carried in the corpus and thrown away only at the walk boundary), reports an SCC/cycle census in the returned dict (forward-required once batch-emit makes cycles legal), and partitions today's single `dangling` count into distinct, honest categories (genuine-dangling vs filter-excluded, plus the keyless disclosure). It is a projection-and-render change confined to `commands/fetch.py`, `lenses/graph.py`, the `--edge` arg plumbing in `cli/`, and the graph tests/goldens; domain composition (capability/flow/stage views) is explicitly out of scope.

files.role: PRIMARY — fetch_graph (def at line 966) + _longest_chains (848) + _top_chains (933). Widen signature to accept key/edge; add global-node-set fetch for (e) classification; retain predicates in DFS; add SCC census; split dangling counters in the returned dict (1090-1103).

PRIMARY — graph lens. Widen module-level fetch (45-49) to accept key/edge and forward. Extend graph_view (95) + _chain_line (74-92) to render per-hop predicate labels, the new dangling/filter-excluded/keyless breakdown on the counts line (52-60, 202-207, 306-313), and the cycle census section. fold_view re-export (329) unchanged.
SECONDARY — add `--edge` argument (after --key, ~line 88) with a predicate completer stub. Declaration-only; parsed by the fold view.

SECONDARY — thread args.edge into _build_fold_fetch (391-438); pass edge= ONLY on the call_lens_fetch branch (418-428), never to fetch_fold. Optionally refuse `--edge` when the resolved lens fetch does not accept it, reusing the _lens_fetch_accepts_cursor idiom (367-388).
OPTIONAL — a complete_edge completer (predicate names from the vertex's census/declared edge fields), mirroring complete_key. Skip if deferring completion.

TESTS — extend TestFetch/TestTraversal/TestZooms with key-honoring, --edge filtering, chain predicate retention, SCC census, and dangling/filter-excluded/keyless partition cases. 37 tests pass at baseline.
GOLDENS — the 8 [*-graph] snapshot dirs change (chains line gains predicate labels; counts line gains the new breakdown). Regenerate with --update-goldens after impl.

REFERENCE (slice-1 territory, do NOT reshape here) — inbound_edges field (132), _edge_corpus (152-180), _address_matches_key (274-276), _compute_inbound_edges (279-300). fetch_graph reads surface.inbound_edges + Row.address; these become Address(kind,key)-typed under slice 1.

current_behavior: `fetch_graph(vertex_path, *, kind=None, observer=None)` (fetch.py:966) projects the store as a directed graph. It calls `project(fetch_fold(vertex_path, kind=kind, observer=observer))` (fetch.py:1008) — note NO key param. The graph lens's own `fetch(vertex_path, kind=None, observer=None)` (lenses/graph.py:45-49) also omits key. Because `call_lens_fetch` (lens_resolver.py:513-540) passes only kwargs the fetch signature names, `_build_fold_fetch`'s `key=` (fold.py:422) is SILENTLY DROPPED for the graph lens. Verified on the live project vertex: `sl read project --lens graph --json` and `... --key architecture/ --json` are byte-identical (nodes 1312 / edges 1765 / dangling 166 / orphans 485). Single `--key` also escapes the dispatch inert-transform note because `_spec_has_dropped_transforms` (dispatch.py:105-131) excludes `queried_key`. `--kind` IS honored (fetch-level filter) but conflates: `--kind decision` gives dangling 310 (vs 166 unfiltered) because refs to kind-excluded-but-existing nodes are counted as `dangling` (fetch.py:1033-1034: `dangling = total_outbound - resolved_edges`). Chain paths are `list[str]` of addresses only — the DFS discards the predicate at fetch.py:902 (`targets = sorted({t for t, _ in adjacency.get(node, ())})`), so `_chain_line` (lenses/graph.py:74-92) renders `a → b → c` with no edge labels. Cycles are guarded (per-path back-edge skip, fetch.py:904) but never reported — no census key. The returned dict (fetch.py:1090-1103) exposes `dangling` and `unsourced_inbound` as single scalars with no dangling/filter-excluded/keyless breakdown and no `cycles`/`sccs` key. Graph tests (37) pass at baseline.

planned_changes.description: Widen `fetch_graph(vertex_path, *, kind=None, key=None, edge=None, observer=None)` and the graph lens `fetch(vertex_path, kind=None, key=None, edge=None, observer=None)` to accept key. Forward key into the node projection. RECOMMENDED shape: keep the in-scope node projection filtered by kind+key (matches current --kind behavior — pass key to fetch_fold OR filter Surface rows post-project), AND additionally fetch the FULL unfiltered vertex once (`fetch_fold(vertex_path, observer=obs)` → project → `global_node_addrs = {r.address for r in rows}`) purely to power the (e) classification. `call_lens_fetch` will now pass key to the widened graph fetch (honored); if a future non-graph composition fetch lacks a key param it still silently drops — that is fine for graph. For the honor-or-refuse posture on the CLI edge (e.g. --key on a lens whose fetch cannot honor it), the existing _lens_fetch_accepts_cursor refusal idiom (fold.py:367) is the template.

Add `--edge` to read_args.py (metavar=PREDICATE, comma-OR grammar mirroring --key; help: 'Restrict the graph to edges of this predicate (ref, or a declared typed-edge field; comma-OR)'). Thread args.edge through fold.py `_build_fold_fetch` into the `call_lens_fetch(...)` call ONLY (add `edge=edge`), NOT into the `fetch_fold(...)` fallback branch (fetch_fold has no edge param). In fetch_graph, when edge is set, restrict the outbound adjacency build (fetch.py:1015-1029) and census to edges whose `pred` is in the edge set — hubs re-rank by the filtered inbound, chains follow filtered edges, census lists only the selected predicate(s). Name deliberately avoids 'predicate' (owned by the inline field=value eq grammar).

planned_changes.step: (c) Retain predicate labels through the DFS
planned_changes.description: Change the chain representation to carry the edge predicate per hop. In `_longest_chains` (fetch.py:848), stop collapsing `{t for t, _ in ...}` at line 902 — walk `(target, predicate)` and record the predicate that entered each node. Emit chains as list of hops carrying (address, predicate_into_this_node) — e.g. path stays `list[str]` plus a parallel `predicates: list[str|None]` (first entry None, one per edge). Propagate through `_top_chains` (fetch.py:933) subpath logic (compare on address path only; carry predicates alongside) and the returned `chains` entries (fetch.py:1080, 1101). In `_chain_line` (lenses/graph.py:74-92) render `a --ref--> b --blocks--> c` (or a chosen glyph) instead of bare `→`; keep the shed-to-`a → … → c` fallback and the truncated/leaf tails.

planned_changes.step: (d) SCC/cycle census in the returned dict
planned_changes.description: Add a strongly-connected-component pass (Tarjan or iterative Kosaraju, iterative to avoid recursion limits at 1300+ nodes) over the resolved `outbound` adjacency (fetch.py:1015-1029) AFTER it is built. Report non-trivial SCCs (size>1, plus self-loops) as a new dict key (proposed `cycles: [[addr, ...], ...]` or `sccs` with count) at fetch.py:1090-1103. Render a small census section in graph_view at DETAILED+ (mirroring the EDGES/ORPHANS sections) disclosing cycle count and members. On the live vertex today this should report 0 (near-DAG); the value is forward-required for batch-emit (thread:ref-graph-dag-assumption-audit).

Replace the single `dangling = total_outbound - resolved_edges` (fetch.py:1033-1034) with a 3-way classification of each UNRESOLVED outbound ref: (1) filter_excluded — the ref's target resolves to a node in `global_node_addrs` (the full-vertex set from step a) but not in the in-scope `node_addrs`; (2) dangling — target resolves nowhere even globally (genuine dead ref, e.g. decision:ghost); (3) keyless — the SOURCE is keyless/collect (already surfaced inbound-side as unsourced_inbound — decide whether to also count outbound-side, see open question). Emit `dangling` (genuine only) + `filter_excluded` as separate counts (and optionally address lists) in the returned dict. Also partition orphans: a node that is isolated in-scope but connected in the full graph is `filter_isolated`, distinct from `orphans` (truly isolated globally) — reuse global_node_addrs + the global inbound_edges to test. Update graph_view counts line (lenses/graph.py:52-60, 202-207, 306-313) to disclose the split honestly.

The graph walk's node-membership tests (`source not in node_addrs`, `target not in node_addrs` at fetch.py:1020-1024) and the (e) classification (`target in global_node_addrs`) are string-set membership TODAY. Slice 1 retypes Row.address, Surface.inbound_edges (surface.py:132), Edge.address (fold_state.py:33) and the corpus matcher _address_matches_key (surface.py:274-276) to Address(kind,key). Structure BOTH membership tests as a single helper (e.g. `_resolves_to_node(addr, node_set)`) so that when slice 1 lands, the classification switches from suffix-string matching to Address equality (kind AND key) in ONE place — this is exactly the aliasing the slice-1 hypothesis flags (cross-kind key aliasing via suffix-only match). If slice 1 has already landed when this is implemented, build the helper directly on Address equality.

The 8 tests.golden.test_grammar_parity[*-graph] snapshots change (chains line gains predicate labels from (c); counts line gains the dangling/filter-excluded breakdown from (e); a cycle-census line may appear). Run `uv run --package loops pytest apps/loops/tests/golden --update-goldens` and read the diff as the drift report (conftest.py:49 supports the flag).

test_plan: Unit (fetch_graph key honoring): build a fixture where --key selects a subgraph; assert `fetch_graph(vp, key='...')` returns FEWER nodes than unfiltered (proves the silent-drop is gone) and that the excluded-but-referenced targets land in filter_excluded, not dangling.

Unit (--edge filtering): fixture with mixed ref + a declared typed edge (e.g. blocks); assert `fetch_graph(vp, edge='blocks')` census/hubs/chains contain only blocks edges and `edge='ref'` excludes the typed edge. Reuse the grammar fixture (write_grammar_fixture) which already has one typed edge candidate.

Unit (chain predicate retention): extend TestTraversal — assert a chain over mixed predicates carries the per-hop predicate labels (a→(ref)→b→(blocks)→c), and that _top_chains subpath-dedup still keys on the address path.

Unit (SCC census): feed _longest_chains/fetch_graph a cyclic adjacency (a→b→c→a) and assert the returned dict reports the SCC {a,b,c}; assert a pure DAG reports zero cycles; assert the existing cycle-does-not-hang guarantee still holds (test_cycle_does_not_hang, test_cycle_memo_not_poisoned_by_visit_order must stay green).

Unit (dangling partition): extend the _dangling_fixture (decision:ghost is genuine-dangling) with a case where a --kind/--key filter excludes an EXISTING target; assert dangling counts only decision:ghost and filter_excluded counts the excluded-but-existing target. Assert the arithmetic still reconciles (edges + unsourced_inbound == summed hub inbound stays true; add a reconciliation assert for the new split).

Register parity: extend the existing assert_register_parity graph test so the new counts-line breakdown and chain predicate labels appear faithfully on BOTH the piped and TTY registers (the graph lens is register-split — this is the standing requirement in apps/loops/CLAUDE.md).

Golden: run `uv run --package loops pytest apps/loops/tests/golden -k graph` after --update-goldens; eyeball the diff to confirm only intended changes (predicate labels + counts breakdown), no accidental drift.
Full gate: `uv run --package loops pytest apps/loops/tests` green (baseline 37 in test_graph.py + goldens).

Live smoke via installed CLI (per CLAUDE.md — run `uv tool install . -e` first): `sl read project --lens graph --key architecture/ --json` must now differ from the unfiltered run (nodes shrink), `sl read project --lens graph --edge ref` restricts the census, and `--kind decision --json` dangling drops sharply as filter_excluded absorbs the ~310-166 conflation.
acceptance_criteria: `sl read project --lens graph --key architecture/` is NO LONGER byte-identical to the unfiltered graph — --key is honored (node set shrinks to the architecture/ prefix), closing friction:graph-fetch-drops-key.
A --key/--edge that cannot be honored is refused with a teaching message (honor-or-refuse, the 184dfce posture), never silently dropped.
`--edge <predicate>` restricts hubs, chains, and census to the selected edge predicate(s); the name does not collide with the inline field=value 'predicate' grammar.
Chains render per-hop predicate labels on both registers (e.g. a --ref--> b --blocks--> c), retained through the DFS rather than discarded at the walk boundary.
The returned dict carries an SCC/cycle census; a near-DAG reports zero, a cyclic fixture reports the component — and the existing no-hang cycle guard is preserved.

The returned dict splits the former single `dangling` into genuine-dangling vs filter-excluded (and discloses keyless/unsourced honestly); on `--kind decision` the genuine-dangling count is far below today's 310, with the difference attributed to filter_excluded.
Register parity holds for all new fields; grammar-parity goldens regenerated with only intended diffs; full apps/loops test suite green.
Node-membership + classification go through a single helper so slice 1's Address(kind,key) retyping swaps string-suffix matching for Address equality in one place.
risks: Behavior change to the EXISTING --kind path: today --kind decision reports dangling=310; after (e) most of that becomes filter_excluded. This is the intended fix (the 268-conflation the design cites) but it changes a shipped output shape — the graph goldens and any downstream consumer of the flat `dangling` scalar must be updated in the same change (dissolution-sweep the residue).

Inbound-count / chain / tier scope under a filter stays SUB-SCOPE (a filtered node's ←N counts only in-scope sources, because project() computes the corpus over the filtered FoldState). This is a pre-existing caveat (documented for tiers at surface.py:532) and is NOT changed here — but combined with the new global-node-set classification it can look inconsistent (global for dangling/orphan classification, sub-scope for counts). Document it as named residue, or resolve per the open question below.

Adding a second full-vertex fetch (for global_node_addrs) doubles the fold cost of a filtered graph read. On the 1312-node live vertex the fold is fast (<1s), but note the extra pass; a single unfiltered project + in-memory scope-filter (global-compute approach) would avoid the double fetch if the arbiter chooses that shape.

Chain representation change (list[str] → path + predicates) ripples through _top_chains subpath dedup and every chains-consumer (test_graph.py assertions compare exact chain dicts, the golden parity harness, _chain_line). Keep `path` a plain address list and add predicates as a PARALLEL field to minimize breakage to existing `{path, truncated}` consumers.
SCC over 1300+ nodes must be iterative — a recursive Tarjan risks Python's recursion limit (the same reason _longest_chains has a depth cap of 128).

`--edge` given without `--lens graph` has no meaning on the default fold route; if not explicitly refused it silently no-ops (the very failure mode this slice fixes for --key). Decide the without-graph behavior (see open questions).
dependencies: Slice 1 (typed-address, Address(kind,key)) — hypothesis:refs-as-typed-address-dataclass. Reshapes the address-string sites this walk reads: Row.address, Surface.inbound_edges (surface.py:132), Edge.address (fold_state.py:33), and the suffix-only matcher _address_matches_key (surface.py:274-276). This slice must route node-membership and the (e) classification through a single helper so the swap to Address equality is one-line when slice 1 lands. Not a hard blocker — can be built on today's strings if slice 1 is not yet merged — but the helper structure is mandatory to avoid rework.

184dfce (read-router temporal-flag refusal) — the honor-or-refuse idiom; test template at apps/loops/tests/test_read_router_temporal_guard.py. The runtime analogue for lens fetches is _lens_fetch_accepts_cursor (fold.py:367).
thread:ref-graph-dag-assumption-audit (open) — item (d) is the forward-required half: cycles become legal once batch-emit ships; the census makes them visible.
painted (PyPI) rendering primitives used by graph_view (Block, join_vertical, Style, Zoom) — no version bump required; the chain-label and counts-line changes are pure loops-side lens edits.
open_questions: FILTER SEMANTICS FORK: when --key/--kind narrows the graph, are hub inbound counts, chains, and tiers computed over the in-scope SUB-GRAPH (current --kind behavior) or over the FULL graph with the scope applied only as a display/classification overlay? Item (e)'s dangling-vs-filter-excluded split REQUIRES the global node set either way, but whether inbound/chains go global is a real fork. RECOMMENDATION: keep node projection sub-scope (least surprising, matches shipped --kind), add the full-vertex node set solely for (e) classification. Confirm, or choose global-compute (single projection, scope as overlay — cleaner but changes ←N semantics under a filter).

OUTBOUND-KEYLESS TAXONOMY: item (e) says 'partition orphans by keyless-vs-dangling'. `keyless` (source has no address) is today disclosed INBOUND-side as `unsourced_inbound`. Should the outbound-unresolved partition ALSO carry a `keyless` bucket (source-keyless refs), or does keyless stay purely an inbound-side disclosure and the outbound split be just {dangling, filter_excluded}? This decides the exact dict-key set — arbiter-level because it fixes the wire contract.

--edge WITHOUT --lens graph: refuse (honor-or-refuse, consistent with 184dfce), silently no-op, or emit the dispatch inert-transform note? RECOMMENDATION: refuse with a teaching message pointing at --lens graph, since silent no-op is the exact defect class this slice eliminates. Confirm the posture.
measures: genuine-dangling vs filter_excluded counts on `--kind decision` (today: 310 conflated; target: genuine << 310)
cycle/SCC count on the live project vertex (expected 0, near-DAG)
nodes returned for `--lens graph --key architecture/` (today 1312 = silent-drop; target: shrinks to the architecture/ subset)
LOC delta of the classification helper (single chokepoint for slice-1 Address swap)
